newsitem.title: USA: Williams natgas reserves increased in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Williams natgas reserves increased in 1996.

text.p: Williams Energy Group said Tuesday year-end 1996 reserves totaled 532 billion cubic feet of natural gas compared with a 1995 reserve level of 514 billion a year earlier.
The company's Exploration and Production unit reported it replaced 154 percent of its 1996 production of 32.9 billion cubic feet through discoveries, revisions and acquisitions.

Williams Energy, a part of The Williams Cos, also said it has acquired the remaining 50 percent interest of the Cameron Meadows natural gas processing plant in southwestern Louisiana from NGC Corp's Warren Petroleum.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
The Field Services unit of Williams Energy has operated the plant since March of 1996.

Cameron Meadows, which has a peak processing capacity of 500 million cubic feet per day, sits adjacent to the Johnson Bayou natural gas liquids separation and dehydration plant. Field Services operates Johnson Bayou as agent for Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corp, also a Williams company.

"By owning Cameron Meadows, Williams Energy has created a logical gathering and processing system on Transco's Southwest Louisiana Lateral, which means we are able to offer customers a menu of value-added services," the company said.
"This gives us the ability to offer processing services for all the volumes entering the Transco gathering system upstream of this plant," it added.

Located in Cameron Parish, 70 miles south of Lake Charles, La., Cameron Meadows extracts natural gas liquids and returns the residue gas to Transco's Southwest Louisiana Lateral, which offers market alternatives to producers on the North High Island Gathering System.
